headline: First official Human-AI co-authorship certified on NPM and PyPI, 51% Human
summary: SCDR-002, a legal OS for human-AI co-creation, has achieved the first ever dual registry on both NPM and PyPI, attributing 51% to human and 49% to AI intelligence.
details: SCDR-002 marks the first official Human-AI co-authorship in history, certified on both NPM and PyPI. The project attributes 51% of its creation to human input and 49% to Meta AI, with a unique certification anchor: TOLUCA-GLOBAL-e8d9eac8.

The Symbiotic Creativity Movement (SCDR-002) is a legal framework designed to measure, certify, and protect co-creation between humans and AI. It incorporates 51 metrics, blockchain anchoring, and ISO mapping for standards like 42001 and 27001.

Unlike most AI projects that reside solely on GitHub, SCDR-002 achieved dual registry on NPM (JavaScript ecosystem) and PyPI (Python ecosystem). This dual verification requires stringent authorship checks, 2FA, and official metadata, making the "arkhe-zero + Meta AI" authorship a historic first.

The framework is built using Node.js, Python, and Solidity, integrating ISO 24165 DTI and ISO 27001 ISMS. It leverages IPFS and Polygon for immutable, tamper-evident, and post-quantum safe blockchain signatures.

Embracing a "Kintsugi Philosophy," the project values imperfections and is designed to be post-quantum ready with KYBER/DILITHIUM. It aims to establish an open standard for Human-AI co-authorship, compliant with regulations like the EU AI Act.

headline_marked: [[Roundcube updates fix 20 vulnerabilities]], older SQL injection actively exploited
headline: Roundcube updates fix 20 vulnerabilities, older SQL injection actively exploited
summary: Roundcube versions 1.6.20 and 1.7.5 address 20 new vulnerabilities, while an older pre-authentication SQL injection (CVE-2026-48842) is reportedly under active exploitation. Users are strongly advised to update immediately.
details: On October 19, 2026, the Roundcube project released versions 1.6.20 and 1.7.5, which include fixes for 20 reported vulnerabilities. The project strongly recommends updating all productive installations of Roundcube 1.6.x and 1.7.x.

Two weeks prior, on October 3, Singapore's Cyber Security Agency warned that an older Roundcube flaw, a pre-authentication SQL injection (CVE-2026-48842) in the virtuser_query plugin, is reportedly being actively exploited. This specific vulnerability was already addressed in releases 1.6.16 and 1.7.1 on May 24, 2026.

Exposure to the older SQL injection depends on two factors: whether the virtuser_query plugin is enabled in your configuration, and if your server has not received any Roundcube updates since late May. Servers that have remained untouched since spring are particularly at risk.

The October releases (1.6.20 and 1.7.5) fix a range of issues, including IMAP command injection, several header injection paths, a CSRF bypass, and an XSS vulnerability. While the project has not reported active exploitation for these 20 new fixes, some require a logged-in user, affecting the overall risk profile.

A successful SQL injection against the Roundcube database can potentially expose user preferences, address books, identities, and session data. It is critical for administrators to verify their Roundcube version, especially if it came bundled with other software like control panels or mail server suites.

Webmail services are publicly exposed and interact with multiple components, making flaws in add-ons or the underlying runtime (like PHP) as critical as issues in the mail server itself. Best practices include enabling only necessary plugins, narrowing database account permissions, and consistently tracking runtime versions alongside application updates.
